frame.his_words: we quit 70-25 things and adopt new frame work of 1-10-8-40

containers.name: Homeostasis and Allostasis
containers.filters: Illness, environment, exertion, nutrition, hydration, age, chronic stress, medication
containers.note: Homeostasis corrects present imbalance; allostasis anticipates future need. Either can override conscious intention.

containers.name: Arousal and Wakefulness
containers.filters: Sleep loss, threat, novelty, caffeine, medication, time of day, stress, boredom
containers.note: Sets how much processing capacity is available at a given moment; too little or too much both degrade performance.

containers.name: Sleep and Circadian Regulation
containers.filters: Light exposure, routine, age, stress, substances, illness, shift work, environment
containers.note: Sleep is not inactivity; it reshapes learning, emotion, attention and memory availability.

containers.name: Interoception and Internal Body Mapping
containers.filters: Attention, anxiety, expectation, illness, body awareness, trauma, training, cultural interpretation
containers.note: Converts bodily signals into experienced states such as discomfort, calm, urgency or 'gut feeling.'

containers.name: Autonomic and Hormonal Regulation
containers.filters: Acute stress, chronic stress, sex, age, medication, menstrual cycle, pregnancy, illness
containers.note: Alters emotion, risk-taking, attention, aggression, bonding and effort without requiring conscious approval.

containers.name: Pain and Protective Signalling
containers.filters: Attention, expectation, fear, context, past injury, social support, fatigue, medication
containers.note: Pain is not simply an incoming signal; interpretation and context change the experienced result.

containers.name: Energy, Fatigue and Resource Budgeting
containers.filters: Sleep, nutrition, illness, workload, reward, mood, motivation, fitness
containers.note: Determines whether a person deploys available capacity, not merely whether capacity exists.

containers.name: Basic Biological Drives
containers.filters: Deprivation, hormones, culture, age, safety, relationship state, goals, inhibition
containers.note: Foundational motive sources, but shaped, not simply controlled, by cognition and culture.

containers.name: Visual Perception
containers.filters: Lighting, attention, expectation, expertise, eyesight, fatigue, emotion, context
containers.note: The same image can produce different meanings depending on expectation, attention and experience.

containers.name: Auditory Perception
containers.filters: Noise, language familiarity, hearing ability, attention, emotion, expectation, age
containers.note: Separates meaningful sources from competing noise and links sound to probable causes.

containers.name: Somatosensory Perception
containers.filters: Attention, injury, body location, emotional state, expectation, neurological condition
containers.note: Provides both environmental information and continuous feedback about the body.

containers.name: Smell, Taste and Chemical Sensing
containers.filters: Hunger, illness, culture, prior exposure, hormones, age, expectation
containers.note: Strongly connected with memory, appetite, threat avoidance and emotional association.

containers.name: Multisensory Integration
containers.filters: Timing, reliability of each sense, attention, context, prior belief, sensory impairment
containers.note: Produces one coherent experience from multiple incomplete and sometimes conflicting signals.

containers.name: Salience and Orienting
containers.filters: Personal goals, fear, reward history, trauma, novelty, social meaning, current task
containers.note: Determines what receives priority before detailed reasoning begins.

containers.name: Body Schema, Body Image and Ownership
containers.filters: Vision, touch, culture, injury, social comparison, trauma, movement, body beliefs
containers.note: Separates 'my body,' 'near my body,' and 'external object.' Body image adds beliefs and evaluation.

containers.name: Spatial, Temporal and Environmental Mapping
containers.filters: Familiarity, attention, emotion, speed, age, sensory cues, culture, stress
containers.note: Combines where, when, how far and what comes next into an actionable world model.

containers.name: Action Readiness and Affordance Detection
containers.filters: Body position, environment, skill, fear, fatigue, goals, object familiarity
containers.note: Detects what actions are presently possible before selecting one.

containers.name: Motor Planning and Sequencing
containers.filters: Skill, object properties, time pressure, fatigue, injury, attention
containers.note: Converts an intended physical outcome into an ordered movement programme.

containers.name: Motor Execution and Control
containers.filters: Strength, fatigue, injury, stress, practice, feedback, environment
containers.note: Executes the selected plan while continuously adjusting movement.

containers.name: Action Selection and Initiation
containers.filters: Reward, threat, habit, instruction, hesitation, social permission, confidence
containers.note: Answers: which action should begin now?

containers.name: Coordination, Balance and Posture
containers.filters: Surface, vision, vestibular input, fatigue, age, illness, intoxication
containers.note: Maintains bodily stability while perception and action continue.

containers.name: Procedural Skill and Automatization
containers.filters: Practice quality, feedback, sleep, motivation, injury, task consistency
containers.note: Converts effortful performance into faster, less consciously demanding action.

containers.name: Imitation, Gesture and Tool Manipulation
containers.filters: Social attention, familiarity, culture, motor capacity, intention understanding
containers.note: Supports learning from others and using objects as extensions of action.

containers.name: Sensorimotor Feedback and Error Correction
containers.filters: Feedback delay, sensory reliability, fatigue, practice, injury, attention
containers.note: Runs a rapid intention -> action -> actual outcome -> correction loop.

containers.name: Selective Attention
containers.filters: Salience, motivation, fatigue, noise, anxiety, task demand, expertise
containers.note: Selects one stream for deeper processing while reducing competing input.

containers.name: Sustained Attention and Vigilance
containers.filters: Boredom, sleep, duration, reward, stress, task frequency, environment
containers.note: Maintains attention when important events are rare or delayed.

containers.name: Divided Attention and Attention Switching
containers.filters: Task similarity, complexity, practice, urgency, fatigue, working-memory load
containers.note: Humans normally switch rather than fully process many difficult tasks simultaneously.

containers.name: Working Memory
containers.filters: Load, distraction, stress, sleep, age, expertise, chunking
containers.note: Holds active information needed for immediate reasoning and action.

containers.name: Inhibitory Control and Self-Control
containers.filters: Reward size, fatigue, stress, habit strength, social monitoring, values
containers.note: Suppresses a dominant response when another goal has higher priority.

containers.name: Cognitive Flexibility
containers.filters: Rigidity, stress, expertise, uncertainty, emotional investment, time pressure
containers.note: Allows the person to leave a failing interpretation or strategy.

containers.name: Executive Sequencing and Task Management
containers.filters: Complexity, experience, time, working memory, tools, motivation
containers.note: Coordinates multiple cognitive and physical operations toward a result.

containers.name: Conflict, Error and Performance Monitoring
containers.filters: Feedback quality, overconfidence, fatigue, stakes, emotion, accountability
containers.note: Detecting an error and accepting an error are separate functions.

containers.name: Episodic Memory
containers.filters: Emotion, attention during event, sleep, age, rehearsal, trauma, similarity
containers.note: Stores what happened to me, where and when. It is reconstructive, not a perfect recording.

containers.name: Semantic Memory and General Knowledge
containers.filters: Education, experience, language, retrieval frequency, misinformation, age
containers.note: Stores decontextualised knowledge without requiring recollection of the original learning event.

containers.name: Procedural and Habit Memory
containers.filters: Repetition, reinforcement, context stability, motivation, interruption
containers.note: Can guide behaviour without conscious verbal recall.

containers.name: Associative Learning and Conditioning
containers.filters: Timing, repetition, intensity, fear, reward, context change
containers.note: Learns that one event predicts another, even without explicit reasoning.

containers.name: Reinforcement and Reward Learning
containers.filters: Reward delay, uncertainty, effort, prior outcome, social reward, deprivation
containers.note: Updates behaviour based on differences between expected and actual outcomes.

containers.name: Emotional and Threat Memory
containers.filters: Intensity, trauma, repetition, context, regulation, extinction exposure
containers.note: Emotion can strengthen some aspects of memory while distorting or narrowing others.

containers.name: Prospective Memory
containers.filters: Delay, cues, interruption, priority, planning tools, fatigue
containers.note: Stores what I must remember to do later, not only past experience.

containers.name: Encoding, Consolidation, Retrieval, Reconsolidation and Forgetting
containers.filters: Attention, sleep, cues, repetition, emotion, age, similarity, misinformation
containers.note: Every retrieval can potentially modify the memory that is later stored again.

containers.name: Concept Formation and Abstraction
containers.filters: Experience, language, culture, goals, examples, exceptions, expertise
containers.note: Converts individual experiences into reusable concepts and categories.

containers.name: Core Reasoning
containers.filters: Knowledge quality, working memory, bias, motivation, time, emotion, intelligence, instruction
containers.note: No single reasoning mode is universally correct; the task determines the required mode.

containers.name: Causal, Counterfactual and Predictive Reasoning
containers.filters: Data quality, temporal order, prior belief, complexity, hidden variables, experience
containers.note: Distinguishes correlation from causation and imagines alternative histories or futures.

containers.name: Uncertainty, Probability and Confidence
containers.filters: Numeracy, emotion, stakes, framing, prior belief, experience, overconfidence
containers.note: Felt certainty and actual accuracy can differ significantly.

containers.name: Problem Framing and Decomposition
containers.filters: User wording, expertise, assumptions, incentives, available evidence, time
containers.note: A wrong problem frame can produce a correct solution to the wrong problem.

containers.name: Planning, Strategy and Future Simulation
containers.filters: Time horizon, uncertainty, resources, motivation, experience, social dependence
containers.note: Builds a model of actions and likely consequences before execution.

containers.name: Decision, Judgment and Trade-off Intelligence
containers.filters: Values, emotion, social pressure, framing, scarcity, information, authority
containers.note: Humans alternate between habitual, intuitive, deliberative and socially influenced choices.

containers.name: Creativity, Imagination and Invention
containers.filters: Knowledge breadth, mood, inhibition, working memory, culture, safety, reward
containers.note: Creativity needs both generation and selection; novelty alone is not usefulness.

containers.name: Speech and Language-Signal Recognition
containers.filters: Noise, accent, familiarity, hearing, literacy, attention, language exposure
containers.note: Converts continuous sound or visual symbols into probable language units.

containers.name: Lexical and Semantic Access
containers.filters: Context, language, culture, frequency, expertise, priming, age
containers.note: A word activates multiple possible meanings before context suppresses weaker interpretations.

containers.name: Syntax and Grammar
containers.filters: Language, dialect, complexity, working memory, education, exposure
containers.note: Organises words into relational structures rather than isolated meanings.

containers.name: Comprehension and Discourse Integration
containers.filters: Context length, background knowledge, attention, ambiguity, trust, working memory
containers.note: Builds one situation model from many statements.

containers.name: Language Production and Articulation
containers.filters: Emotion, time pressure, audience, language proficiency, fatigue, social risk
containers.note: Converts internal meaning into an external linguistic sequence.

containers.name: Pragmatics and Implied Meaning
containers.filters: Relationship, culture, power, tone, shared knowledge, setting
containers.note: What was said and what was meant may differ.

containers.name: Prosody, Gesture and Non-Verbal Communication
containers.filters: Culture, emotion, personality, relationship, masking, environment
containers.note: Non-verbal signals can reinforce, weaken or contradict spoken language.

containers.name: Narrative, Reading, Writing and Audience Adaptation
containers.filters: Purpose, audience, literacy, status, trust, format, medium
containers.note: Communication success is measured by the receiver's usable understanding, not only sender accuracy.

containers.name: Emotion Generation and Affective State
containers.filters: Body state, interpretation, memory, culture, relationships, hormones, environment
containers.note: Emotion is a multi-component state, not merely a verbal label.

containers.name: Emotion Recognition and Labelling
containers.filters: Interoceptive accuracy, culture, language, masking, attention, social experience
containers.note: A person may experience an emotion without accurately identifying or naming it.

containers.name: Emotion Regulation and Coping
containers.filters: Stress intensity, skill, social support, fatigue, trauma, culture, time
containers.note: Regulation can change the emotion, its expression, its meaning or the resulting behaviour.

containers.name: Positive Valence and Reward
containers.filters: Deprivation, novelty, delay, social approval, personality, prior reward, effort
containers.note: Wanting, liking and learning from reward should be treated separately.

containers.name: Negative Valence, Threat and Loss
containers.filters: Trauma, uncertainty, controllability, proximity, social support, prior learning
containers.note: Threat response can prioritise speed and safety over accuracy or long-term planning.

containers.name: Motivation, Effort and Persistence
containers.filters: Reward, fatigue, confidence, identity, social pressure, probability of success
containers.note: Capability does not guarantee action; expected value and effort cost influence deployment.

containers.name: Intent Formation and Commitment
containers.filters: Motive, authority, opportunity, resources, social consequence, uncertainty
containers.note: Intent answers what the person plans to do. It does not by itself reveal why.

containers.name: Motive, Needs, Values and Priority Structure
containers.filters: Biology, personality, history, culture, reward, threat, relationship, identity
containers.note: Motive answers why. Inferred motive must remain a hypothesis until supported or confirmed.

containers.name: Conscious Awareness and Global Access
containers.filters: Sleep, anaesthesia, attention, brain state, sensory strength, expectation
containers.note: Consciousness is not identical to attention, intelligence, language or memory.

containers.name: Self-Model, Identity and Narrative Self
containers.filters: Memory, culture, relationships, age, trauma, feedback, values
containers.note: The self-model is continuously reconstructed from body, memory and social information.

containers.name: Personality and Temperament
containers.filters: Genetics, development, culture, environment, stress, learning, life events
containers.note: Personality describes tendencies, not fixed behaviour in every condition.

containers.name: Agency, Ownership and Responsibility
containers.filters: Prediction, feedback, coercion, social norms, mental state, body state
containers.note: I acted, I intended, and I caused the result are related but separable judgments.

containers.name: Theory of Mind and Social Prediction
subs: Second-order ToM (they think that I think)
containers.filters: Familiarity, emotion, stereotypes, culture, cognitive load, power
containers.note: Models what another person sees, knows, believes, wants or intends.

containers.name: Empathy, Compassion and Emotional Sharing
containers.filters: Relationship, similarity, group identity, fatigue, threat, power, culture
containers.note: Feeling another's state, understanding it and deciding to help are different operations.

containers.name: Attachment, Belonging, Status and Group Behaviour
containers.filters: Relationship history, group identity, scarcity, authority, culture, threat
containers.note: Human decisions are often optimised for belonging, status or group survival rather than isolated accuracy.

containers.name: Morality, Norms, Culture and Meaning
containers.filters: Culture, religion, law, group, authority, identity, context, consequence
containers.note: Moral judgment, moral motivation and moral action must be separated; people may judge an act wrong yet still perform it.

containers.name: Development and Maturation
containers.filters: Genetics, nutrition, caregiving, education, trauma, culture, illness
containers.note: Human functions do not appear fully formed; different systems mature at different rates.

containers.name: Plasticity, Skill Acquisition and Learning-to-Learn
containers.filters: Age, repetition, feedback, sleep, motivation, injury, task design
containers.note: Plasticity is constrained; improvement in one trained task may not automatically transfer everywhere.

containers.name: Metacognition and Self-Monitoring
containers.filters: Insight, feedback, mood, expertise, stakes, self-protection, cognitive load
containers.note: Performance and awareness of performance can fail independently.

containers.name: Heuristics, Biases and Cognitive Distortion
containers.filters: Time pressure, emotion, identity, incentives, uncertainty, group influence
containers.note: Biases are not only defects; some are fast shortcuts that become harmful under the wrong conditions.

containers.name: Resilience, Failure Detection and Repair
containers.filters: Support, meaning, resources, trauma, personality, prior recovery, safety
containers.note: Failure can produce repair, avoidance, collapse, learning or defensive denial.

containers.name: Expertise and Domain Adaptation
containers.filters: Practice quality, feedback, domain stability, motivation, recency, overconfidence
containers.note: Expert intuition may be powerful in stable environments but unreliable when conditions change.

containers.name: Social Learning, Teaching and Cultural Transmission
containers.filters: Trust, status, group identity, culture, age, success visibility
containers.note: Humans accumulate knowledge across generations rather than learning only through individual trial.

containers.name: External Cognition, Institutions and Collective Intelligence
containers.filters: Access, literacy, trust, coordination, authority, technology, institutional quality
containers.note: Human intelligence extends into tools, other people and institutions; the individual brain is not the entire operating system.
